claims.claim_vi: The source says a Buy click produces a payment event stored by the payment service; one event can hold several payment orders; the executor stores each order and calls an external PSP; the payment service then updates the wallet and the wallet server stores the balance; the ledger service appends new ledger information; PSPs or banks send nightly settlement files with the account balance and the day's transactions.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Own experiment, 2026-10-19, Python 3 and in-memory SQLite: 1,000 payments across three sellers with a simulated fault between the wallet update and the ledger append in 42 payments; without a transaction all three sellers ended out of balance, wallet exceeding ledger by 193,216 minor units; with one transaction and rollback on fault the difference was 0 for all.
claims.section: Thử nghiệm ví và sổ cái
claims.verified_by: Script run in the session; results copied from output.

claims.claim_vi: Own experiment, reconciliation: a settlement list derived from the same payments with 3 payments removed, 2 amounts changed by 100 and 1 extra payment gave 3 only in ours, 1 only at the PSP, 2 with differing amounts, net difference -25,000 minor units.
claims.verified_by: Script run in the session; the data is randomly generated, not a real rate.

design_notes_vi: Khung một là bốn bước; khung hai là ba chỗ phải khớp. Bài khác góc nhìn với sd-07-012 cùng nguồn.
source_deviations: The lesson shares its source file with sd-07-012 (claimed with --allow-same-source); it does not retell the payment flow but tests wallet and ledger consistency and reconciliation.
The statement that wallet and ledger should be updated in one transaction is the author's conclusion from the experiment, not the source's.
